messages.subject: How to use methylKit directly for region-based differential methylation analysis
messages.subject_clean: How to use methylKit directly for region-based differential methylation analysis
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr Akalin,

I am currently analyzing RRBS data and I would like to ask you two questions regarding your methylKit package, that looks great!
I already summarized my methylation profiles per regions of interest (promoters, CGIs etc.) using scripts from the lab, but I would like to use your methylKit package for differential methylation analysis.
Thus my questions are:
1) Can I use methylKit to analyze methylation differences at the level of regions directly (my coverage is a bit too low to analyze CpGs individually)?
2) How can I coerce my data frame to a methylBase object to go straight to differential methylation testing without performing the initial steps of your pipeline?
I attached an example of data frame if needed.

Thank you very much in advance for your help.
Best regards,

Eric Letouzé
INSERM U1162
Functional genomics of solid tumors
27 rue Juliette Dodu, 75010 Paris
+33 (0)1 53 72 51 98

messages.subject: Re: How to use methylKit directly for region-based differential methylation analysis
messages.subject_clean: How to use methylKit directly for region-based differential methylation analysis
messages.body_plain:
Dear Eric,

> 1) Can I use methylKit to analyze methylation differences at the level of regions directly (my coverage is a bit too low to analyze CpGs individually)?

Yes.

> 2) How can I coerce my data frame to a methylBase object to go straight to differential methylation testing without performing the initial steps of your pipeline?

Here is how you can create a methylBase object from your data.frame (df). You need to fill out sample.ids vector, assembly string, treatment vector, these are self explanatory. They are the same/similar arguments you would use when reading a file.

coverage.index,numCs.index and numTs.index are the the vectors for columns numbers (indeces) for numTs, coverage and numCs values in your data frame. destranded is a TRUE|FALSE value showing if you have stranded information or not. The rest I filled out for you, check if they are correct.

obj=new("methylBase",(df),sample.ids=c(),
         assembly="",context="CpG",
         treatment=c(),coverage.index=c(),
         numCs.index=c(),numTs.index=c(),
         destranded=TRUE,resolution="region" )

You have to make sure everything is correct and data frame has the same structure as in a regular methylBase object

Best,
Altuna

> I attached an example of data frame if needed.
>
> Thank you very much in advance for your help.
> Best regards,
>
> Eric Letouzé
> INSERM U1162
> Functional genomics of solid tumors
> 27 rue Juliette Dodu, 75010 Paris
> +33 (0)1 53 72 51 98
>

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Error in annotate.gr.WithGenicParts
messages.body_plain:
We have to establish if this is because of the read.bismark or there is something downstream from that. it could be that you are getting no differentially methylated regions? or getting methylBase object with nothing in it. Check those things, then try to figure out in which step you are losing the regions/bases. it could be something simple as different chromosome naming conventions for different files, which produce 0 regions/bases at unite() step.

Best,
Altuna

>From reading through threads on the discussion forum, it seems that it is generally recommended to have non overlapping windows when carrying out the tiling analysis. In other words, it appears that most people set the same step size as the window size being used.

Hope this is clear! Id love to get your opinion on this.

Many Thanks

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Tiling analysis-step size
messages.body_plain:
if the windows are overlapping, the tests will not be independent. This could pose a problem for multiple-testing correction methods. q-value related methods could deal with dependency structure (SLIM=T, which is default. This is a variation of q-value method and supposedly handles the dependencies better) according to this. Original q-value paper: http://www.genomine.org/papers/dep.pdf. SLIM paper is referenced in the vignette.

This paper discusses performance of q-value methods under dependency structures: http://www.biomedcentral.com/1471-2105/9/114

So I think the literature suggests you can use the overlapping windows and multiple testing correction might deal with that, but we haven't tested this rigorously in our case.

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] calculateDiffMeth when P=0
messages.body_plain:
how are you filtering the locations with P=0  or P=1? If you are referring to the cases where all the methylation values are 0 or 1 (or 100%) across all samples, this is a known issue and you can ignore the warning, you will probably get p-value =1 for those cases. If that is not the case, maybe you can try to provide a reproducible example.

Best
Altuna
